question.problem:
$$ \{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=4{x}_{1}(t)-{x}_{2}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=-4{x}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}(t),\end{aligned}\,x(0)=[\begin{aligned}9 \\ -5\end{aligned}] $$ Consider the initial value problem above. By applying the Laplace transform to both sides of each equation in our system, we get a transformed system with the solution $$ {X}_{1}(s)=L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}=\frac{4}{5s}+\frac{41}{5(s-5)},\,{X}_{2}(s)=L\{{x}_{2}(t)\}=\frac{16}{5s}-\frac{41}{5(s-5)}. $$ Find the solution to the original initial value problem.
$x(t)=\,\,$ {{field-1}} $\,\,+\,\,$ {{field-2}} $\,\,{e}^{5t}$
{{field-3}} {{field-4}}
question.worked_solution:
To find ${x}_{1}(t)$ and ${x}_{2}(t)$ satisfying the original initial value problem, we apply the inverse Laplace transform to ${X}_{1}(s)$ and ${X}_{2}(s)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) & ={L}^{-1}\{{X}_{1}(s)\} \\  & ={L}^{-1}\{\frac{4}{5s}+\frac{41}{5(s-5)}\} \\  & =\frac{4}{5}\,{L}^{-1}\,\{\frac{1}{s}\}\,+\,\frac{41}{5}\,{L}^{-1}\,\{\frac{1}{s-5}\} \\  & =\frac{4}{5}+\frac{41}{5}{e}^{5t} \\ {x}_{2}(t) & ={L}^{-1}\{{X}_{2}(s)\} \\  & ={L}^{-1}\{\frac{16}{5s}-\frac{41}{5(s-5)}\} \\  & =\frac{16}{5}{L}^{-1}\,\{\frac{1}{s}\}\,-\,\frac{41}{5}\,{L}^{-1}\,\{\frac{1}{s-5}\} \\  & =\frac{16}{5}-\frac{41}{5}{e}^{5t}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the solution to the initial value problem is

$$
x(t)=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{5}+\frac{41}{5}{e}^{5t} \\ \frac{16}{5}-\frac{41}{5}{e}^{5t}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{5} \\ \frac{16}{5}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}\frac{41}{5} \\ -\frac{41}{5}\end{aligned}]{e}^{5t}.
$$
